Mr. Mostafa Zaman Islam, Advocate ------ For the Petitioner 
Mr. Shasti Sarker with Mr. Ellius Ahmed, Advocate ------ For the Opposite Parties
parties:
Md. Mokbul Hssain
Vs.
Md. Umar Ali and others
full_judgment:
9. Mr. Mustafa Zaman Islam, the learned Advocate with Mr. Syed Kamrul Hossain, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the preemptee petitioner has placed the judgment and order of the courts below and submitted that the preemption case is barred by limitation in as much as, the case land was sold by registered deed dated 17.11.2002 but the preemption application field on 5.3.2005 having knowledge on 3.3.2005 but the pre-emptor has not been able to prove his alleged date of knowledge. on the other hand, the learned Advocate submits that the pre-emptor being PW.1 stated in the evidence that he came home after 7 days of the sale and the preemptor, has not produced any witness to corroborate his alleged date of knowledge though in the application for preemption as well as in his evidence stated that he came to know from the local people and none of the local people was produced to corroborate his evidence, but the courts below did not at all consider this material aspect of the case and upon such non consideration allowed, the preemption case which is an error resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He contended further that the courts below quoted the evidence of the OPW.1, pre-emptee without discussing the evidence of PW.1 (preemptor), his witnesses has allowed the preemption beyond the scope of the principle of law and thereby, committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He further submitted that the courts below did not consider the evidence of the witnesses cited by the pre-emptee in as much as the evidence of OPW.1, 2 and 3 and also the evidence of Advocate Commissioner, where from it would be evident that the pre-emptee had developed the land at a substantial expenditure within the sight and knowledge of the preemptor for about 2 years 4 months from the date of the execution of the deed but the courts below did not consider those evidence and allowed the preemption case and thereby, upon misconstrued the evidence committed error of law which is an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. He further contended that the preemptor of the case, ignored the transfer for about 3 years but filed the case after statutory period of limitation and in such circumstances, heavy burden lies on the preemptor to discharge the onus of proof about his knowledge of the transfer of the case land but in this particular case failed to discharge the initial onus in not producing witness as to knowledge from among the local people from whom he allegedly came to know about the transfer to corroborate his evidence and such uncorroborated evidence of PW.1 (pre-emptor) being interested witness cannot be relied but the courts acted under misconception of law as to question of onus of proof regarding knowledge of sale and ignoring such legal aspect of the case have allowed the preemption case which is an error resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. 

 "In this case admittedly the application for pre-emption was after 7 years of transfer and a heavy burden lies on the pre-emptor to discharge the onus of proof that he filed the case within four months from the date of his knowledge. The pre-emptor having failed to discharge the initial onus by adducing cogent and reliable evidence the learned single Judge ought to have held that the application for pre-emption is barred by limitation." In the present case the preemptor opposite party has claimed to have knowledge of the transfer of the case land to the pre-emptor petitioner after six and half years of the transfer. He referred no explanation for such a late knowledge of the transfer of a piece of land, which is contiguous to the land held by him and situated next to his baithak khana and the vendor of the land was not a total stranger to him. Nor did he explain the source of his knowledge of the transfer. So his claim is not credible. As against this, there is in the file the contrary evidence of the vendor and the purchaser of the case land, both of whom categorically stated that the pre-emptor was aware of the transfer of the case land immediately after its transfer. They narrated the circumstances in which the pre-emptor had come to know of the transfer. The trial Court found no wrong with their evidence. So, he should have relied upon their evidence and dismissed the pre-emptor's case on the ground of limitation." 

 19. The petitioner admittedly filed the case 2 years and 6 months from the deed of execution of the deed and 1 year 4/5 months after the registration of the deed under section 60 of the Registration Act and as such, burden heavily lies on the pre-emptor to prove his knowledge but the findings and conclusion have made based on solitary witness, the pre-emptor himself who is an interested witness. It is not necessary to seek, corroboration always from independent sources but in the instant case the preemptor himself stated to have knowledge from the (লোক পরস্পরে), in view of such evidence and since the petitioner filed the case beyond 4 months of the deed of registration of the deed and in such, circumstances the preemptor has to prove the knowledge in order to obtain the preemption by corroborative evidences by disinterested witnesses. It is true that under section 134 of the Evidence Act even on the testimony of the solitary witness judgment can be passed provided his credibility is not shaken but in this case, it is on evidence that the preemptor is the full brother of the seller , resides in the same house, and visited the house within 7 days after execution of the deed and continued to ignore the transfer of the case land to the pre-emptee for such a long period and in view of such evidence on record, it appears that the preemptor had failed to discharge initial onus by producing cogent and reliable evidence as to the knowledge by corroborating evidence. But such disability of proving the case has not been considered at all by the courts below and as such, I am of the view that the application for preemption is barred by limitation. There being a total non consideration as to knowledge by the courts below on this point, the findings and decisions arrived at by the courts below being perverse are not sustainable in law due to non consideration of the material evidence on record. It would be evident from the cross examination made by the pre-emptee as to knowledge the PW.1 admitted that he visited his village home frequently and at first he visited the house after 7 days of the execution of the deed, so it would baffle my comprehension that the preemptor could not have knowledge during a long period from execution of the deed as well as from the date of registration of the deed from his brother though the case land was developed and constructed but and chetal over the case land. It is found further from the evidence of OPW.2, 3 and Advocate Commissioner that the preemptor along with the PW.2 who stated that “নালিশী জমি উচু তবে এখন বাড়ী আছে।” that the pre-emptee after purchase improved the land substantially which was a nul (cultivable) land, but the courts below as it appears did not consider those evidence to its true perspective and arrived at wrong conclusion in not disallowing the pre-emption. It is also evident from the record that the petitioner did not file any objection against the report of the Advocate Commissioner and during cross examination the Advocate Commissioner specifically stated as to the development of chatal but such evidence also was not properly considered by the courts below.
